idea.title: ConvertKit: email marketing for bloggers who sell courses and ebooks

source.text: ConvertKit: email marketing for bloggers who sell courses and ebooks, $29 per month, launch country US. Score it as of 2013-06-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: a solo blogger-developer bootstrapping with $5,000. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug convertkit.

idea.problem: Bloggers who sell courses and ebooks need email tools to grow a list and sell to it; generic ESPs are not built for that.
idea.customer: US bloggers who sell their own ebooks and online courses to an email list
idea.solution: Email marketing software (forms, sequences, broadcasts) focused on selling info products
assumptions: Channel: the founder's own blog and blogger peers (not stated)
Audience size modest, under 10k readers (not stated)
Founder sells his own ebooks, so is his own customer (inferred from 'blogger-developer')
Time per week: full time (not stated)
Evidence limited to sources published on or before 2013-06-01

confidence.note: Archived 2013 pricing pages (AWeber, MailChimp) and a pre-2013 SMB churn benchmark could not be read; CAC and churn are estimates.

gross_margin.note: About **86%**: Stripe $1.14 + SES ~$3.00 per $29 account (estimate, 5,000 subs x 6 sends).

ltv_cac.note: LTV ~$497 vs organic CAC ~$120 = 4.1 (estimate); paid CAC unknown, churn assumed 5%/month.

pricing_power.note: $29 sits above AWeber's ~$19 entry tier and MailChimp free; Sendy undercuts at $40 one-off.

build_effort.note: An ESP with forms, sequences and sending on SES: 2-3 months solo to a usable beta (estimate).

skills_match.note: Blogger-developer: can build the app and is the customer; deliverability ops are new.

capital_needed.note: $5,000 covers hosting and SES; Stripe has no setup or monthly fees. No salary runway.

time_to_mvp.note: About 8-12 weeks to a product a blogger will move a list onto (estimate).

sales_cycle.note: Self-serve monthly card purchase by one decision maker; migration adds a few days.

channel_readiness.note: Own blog plus blogger peers who launch ebooks to their lists; reach size assumed modest.

search_demand.note: US email marketing spend forecast at $2.4B by 2016 (Forrester, 2011); active blogger communities.

trend.note: Info-product economy rising: Udemy $12M Series B (2012), Gumroad (2011), $20k ebook launches.

willingness_to_pay.note: Small businesses already pay: Constant Contact has **555,000** paying customers (10-K, 2012).

free_alternatives.note: MailChimp free covers broadcasts for small lists; course-sales sequences are only partly covered.

competitor_density.note: 20+ ESPs: MailChimp, AWeber, Constant Contact, Infusionsoft ($71M raised), GetResponse, iContact.

differentiation.note: One real angle: built for info-product sellers; MailChimp turns away affiliate marketers. Copyable.

legal_regulatory.note: CAN-SPAM compliance (unsubscribe, address, opt-out honoured) is routine but shared with senders.

platform_dependency.note: Relies on SES and inbox providers; Gmail's Promotions tab (2013-05) may cut launch-email opens.

market_risk.note: Email is a durable channel: spend forecast growing at 10% a year.

skills.note: Builds software and runs a blog that sells products: both halves of the job.

assets.note: A blog audience and peer network help; size unknown, assumed under 10k readers.

interest.note: Founder is his own customer: sells ebooks and feels the pain of current tools (assumption).

sam.reasoning: 30,000 US bloggers selling ebooks/courses (assumed, unsourced) x $29 x 12

som.reasoning: 0.5% of SAM $10.44M = 150 paying accounts x $29 x 12

competitors_found.reasoning: MailChimp, AWeber, Constant Contact, Infusionsoft, GetResponse, Campaign Monitor, Mad Mimi, iContact, Sendy, from research

competitor_price_range.reasoning: MailChimp free tier to Infusionsoft entry; 2013 pricing pages not archived-verified

price.reasoning: price set by the founder in the brief

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: assumed for no-contract very-small-business SaaS; Skok: above 2%/month signals trouble; no pre-2013 benchmark for this segment

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: blog visitor or peer intro to paid account; benchmark assumed, unsourced

cac.reasoning: organic: 8 hours of content, outreach and migration help per customer x $15/hour

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: hosting ~$100 + tools ~$50; 2013 hosting price pages not verified

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 150 / 24.86 = 6.03, rounded up; a $5,000/month founder salary needs ~207 customers

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: 8-12 weeks build + beta with blogger peers

verdict.launch_reason: The founder's blog audience and the info-product economy (Gumroad, Udemy, Stripe) are US-centred.
verdict.cheapest_test: Email 30 blogger peers who sell ebooks: offer a $29/month founding plan with hands-on list migration; count pre-payments in 7 days.
kill_criteria: fewer than 5 of 30 blogger peers commit to pay $29/month by day 7 -> stop
fewer than 3 lists over 1,000 subscribers migrated by day 30 -> rethink the segment
under $1,000 MRR by month 6 -> rethink price or segment

rescue.change: Pre-sell 10 blogger peers at $29 and migrate their lists by hand before building the full app
rescue.why: Raises channel_readiness and time_to_mvp; proves differentiation before code
rescue.requires: 10 blogger peers with lists over 1,000 and a product to sell

rescue.change: Narrow to course sellers: tagging plus sales sequences at $49+/month, priced against Infusionsoft not AWeber
rescue.why: Raises pricing_power and differentiation against generic ESPs
rescue.requires: Building automation and checkout integrations (Gumroad, Stripe)

type_checks.note: No pre-2013 monthly churn benchmark for $29 no-contract SMB SaaS; Skok flags >2%/month as trouble and says very small customers churn more.
Bloggers on AWeber or MailChimp must move lists and rebuild sequences; no dated source on import re-confirmation rules.

narrative.answer: **PIVOT**: real demand and **86%** margins, but a crowded field (Constant Contact 555k customers, Infusionsoft $71M raised) means it lives or dies on pre-selling blogger peers before building.
tldr: The info-product economy is rising and email is the tool bloggers sell with.
The market is crowded with funded, cheaper incumbents; $29 is a premium without proof.
Pre-sell 10 blogger peers before writing the full app.

key_findings.title: Funded incumbents own the category
key_findings.detail: Constant Contact had **555,000** paying customers at end-2012 and Infusionsoft raised **$54M** in 2013-01.

key_findings.title: Info-product sellers are a rising niche
key_findings.detail: Designer-bloggers made **$20,000** in two weeks from one ebook (TNW, 2012); Udemy raised $12M (2012).

key_findings.title: Unit economics work on Amazon SES
key_findings.detail: SES at **$0.10 per 1,000** emails plus Stripe fees leave about **86%** gross margin at $29/month (estimate).

narrative.recommendation: Pre-sell before building: get 10 blogger peers to pay $29/month for a hand-migrated founding plan within 7 days, or drop the idea.
narrative.steelman: Bloggers selling ebooks are a rising, underserved niche: MailChimp turns away affiliate marketers and Infusionsoft is overkill. A developer who is his own customer can ship a focused tool on SES at **86%** margin. The evidence supports demand and margin, not the channel.

premortem.cause: Stuck at a few dozen accounts: peers liked it but stayed on AWeber or MailChimp.
premortem.early_signal: fewer than 5 of 30 peers pre-pay in the first 30 days

premortem.cause: $29 lost against MailChimp free and $19 AWeber; small lists saw no reason to pay more.
premortem.early_signal: more than half of prospects ask for a free tier

premortem.cause: Build and deliverability work took 6 months, burning the $5,000 runway first.
premortem.early_signal: beta not sending live campaigns by week 12

rescue.change: Pre-sell 10 blogger peers at $29 and migrate their lists by hand before building the full app
rescue.why: Raises channel_readiness and time_to_mvp; proves differentiation before code
rescue.requires: 10 blogger peers with lists over 1,000 and a product to sell

rescue.change: Narrow to course sellers: tagging plus sales sequences at $49+/month, priced against Infusionsoft not AWeber
rescue.why: Raises pricing_power and differentiation against generic ESPs
rescue.requires: Building automation and checkout integrations (Gumroad, Stripe)

free_alternative.evidence: MailChimp's free plan covers broadcasts for small lists and Sendy costs $40 one-off on SES, but neither targets course-sales sequences: partial.

strong_competitor.evidence: Constant Contact: **555,000** paying customers (10-K FY2012); Infusionsoft: $71M total funding (2013-01).

graveyard.evidence: Wildbit closed its Newsberry newsletter service on 2012-01-02 because it stayed idle in a crowded field; iContact sold to Vocus for $169M (2012).

no_distribution.evidence: Searched blogger communities and paid search; the founder's own blog and peer bloggers who launch to their lists are a credible route to 10 customers.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: SES $0.10 per 1,000 emails and Stripe 2.9% + $0.30 leave about 86% gross margin at $29 (estimate).

weak_demand.evidence: Demand rising: Udemy $12M Series B (2012-12), Gumroad launched 2011, $20k ebook launches (2012).

legal_platform_risk.evidence: CAN-SPAM duties are routine; Gmail's Promotions tab (2013-05-29) and SES dependency are risks, not blockers.

saturated_wave.evidence: Searched Show HN 2012-06 to 2013-05: about 4-5 adjacent email launches (Userfox, list-capture tools), none a direct clone.

customer.segment: US bloggers selling their own ebooks and courses to an email list of 1k-20k subscribers
customer.pain: Generic ESPs make it hard to segment buyers, run launch sequences and sell; Infusionsoft is expensive and complex.
customer.today: AWeber or MailChimp for the list, Gumroad or e-junkie for checkout.

risks.risk: Peers do not switch from AWeber or MailChimp
Deliverability: one spammy sender hurts shared reputation
risks.mitigation: Vet customers, double opt-in, SES complaint monitoring

risks.risk: Gmail Promotions tab lowers launch-email opens
$5,000 runway ends before ramen profitability (~207 accounts)
risks.mitigation: Keep consulting income; pre-sell annual plans

test_plan.step: List 30 blogger peers who sell ebooks or courses to a list
Write a one-page offer: $29/month founding plan, free hand migration
test_plan.verify: page live with a Stripe payment link

test_plan.step: Email and message each peer personally
Ask for the first month up front

changes.what: Amazon SES makes sending cost $0.10 per 1,000 emails
Stripe lets a solo developer bill cards with no setup or monthly fees
Gumroad lets bloggers sell digital goods with a link
Online courses scale: Udemy raises a $12M Series B
Blogger ebook launches earn $10k-$20k in weeks

why_now.note: Cheap sending, easy billing and a booming info-product niche open a window for a focused tool.

icp.who: US bloggers selling their own ebooks or courses, list of 1k-20k subscribers
icp.pays_for_today: AWeber (~$19/month entry, unverified for 2013) or MailChimp, plus Gumroad at 5% + 30 cents per sale
icp.trigger: Planning a product launch and finding the current ESP cannot segment buyers or run a launch sequence
